resolution: Read the clean baseline (the earlier 3021ms was transient backlog from a parallel FacePainter rebuild). Diagnosis: ~650ms/edit, NO leak (nodes/draws/meshes flat; inst +3/place = the placed piece), host render cheap (paint 14ms, gpu 2.4ms) — so the cost is ~500ms main-thread JS reconcile + the ~90ms deferred snapshot (PLACEFREEZE). Ruled out: the loader's overlay scans (measured 0) and the host. Located the prime suspect for the reconcile: index.tsx placementWorld = assemblePreviewWorld rebuilds the ENTIRE GameState from all placements on every edit (a known O(placements) assembler, deps include  which change each edit), and the loader pane renders placements via the live overlay — so most of that per-edit assembly is likely wasted. Rather than guess-cut into a core assembler (also consumed by compile + the properties panel), timed it and folded the ms into the edit-latency line the user already reads. One edit now shows 'pre N (incl. placementWorld Xms)'. Did NOT touch the snapshot (data-integrity-sensitive SNAPBOOT area, only 14% of cost). Sha e8b9a5b94, cart-side hot-reload. Next: confirm placementWorld is the bulk of pre, then make the loader-pane edit loop stop doing a full GameState reassembly per placement (the heavyweight shipped-product work in the edit loop the user has been calling out).
